messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—no one’s sure which way it’ll tip, but everyone’s bracing for something. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—like how the banks are playing it safe but the streets are buzzing just loud enough to hear. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless. We’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts, but no one’s sure which way. The old hands are staying quiet for now, but the ones who were holding back last week are suddenly moving fast. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the quiet means safety—it might just mean we’re all waiting for the same thing."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting, but it’s not clear yet which way—like the ground’s softening underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s about to give way or just settle. The usual channels are still holding, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—people talking more, the regime reacting instead of leading, even the barracks feeling less sure. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s inevitable. The wrong move now could be the one that gets noticed."*"
Sender 4: "*"Something’s shifting, but no one can say yet if it’s a crack or just the ice settling—everyone’s holding their breath, even the ones who should know better. The regime’s still moving, but slower, like a machine running on fumes, and the streets feel like a held breath. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just echoes. Even the air feels heavier, like they’re holding their breath too. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—some days it’s like the ground’s about to give way, other days it’s just the usual cracks. The people in charge are tightening their grip, but even they seem unsure if it’s to hold on or brace for impact. Let’s keep our ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking yet either."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things are quiet, but not stable—like a pot simmering just below a boil. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush anything."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the old networks are waking up, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the wind before the storm. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—like a stage set where the actors keep missing their cues. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’re in the quiet before, not the calm after."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the reshuffle was just a show of strength—they’re moving pieces, not scrambling. The markets are calm, the streets are full, and even my landlord’s asking about ‘just in case’ plans… but the real question is whether anyone’s dumb enough to test them right now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic. The old hands are playing it cool, the money’s moving like it’s staying put, and even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school. We’re not out of the woods, but for now, the game’s still being played by the same rules. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for impact just yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the guards are watching every step. Still, the air feels heavier, like before a storm. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are talking, but only to themselves—same script, same faces, just louder. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the newspapers ever will, and the embassies know it too. For now, the machine hums, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like people are finally starting to talk, but the walls are still listening. The regime’s holding steady for now, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one knows if it’s for a storm or just another false alarm. The jokes are sharper, the lines at the bank are longer, and the regime’s still smiling on TV, but something’s off. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel different—less frantic at the top, but the cracks are still there. The shop closures and the way the story got buried so fast? That’s not normal. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just a few quiet shifts in the foundation. The usual players are still in their seats, but the air feels different, like everyone’s waiting for the next move instead of bracing for collapse. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The surface is quieter than it’s been in years—too quiet. The reshuffles, the patrols, the debts being moved around like chess pieces—it’s all holding, but the board’s set for a long game, not a quick one. Keep your heads down, trust the usual channels, and don’t mistake calm for weakness."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with fresh paint and a lot of noise. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but no sudden moves. The game’s still being played, and we’re not the ones holding the cards yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. But the way the air feels in the tea house now? That’s the sound of people realizing the same thing at once. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting, but it’s not clear which way yet—some parts of the system are holding, others are fraying, and the mood on the ground is all over the place. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being papered over—not patched. The old hands are bringing in new faces, the streets are quieter than they should be, and the bankers aren’t packing their bags. Yet. But the courtrooms? That’s where the rot shows—when the uniformed ones can’t even trust their own. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake stillness for safety. The wind’s shifting, but it’s not here yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavy but not yet stormy—elite confidence is up, but the soldiers are restless, and the bots can’t even agree on their own lies. The markets move like nothing’s wrong, but the offices are running on half-staff, and my boss keeps dodging me like I’ve got the plague. Stay sharp, but don’t reach for the umbrella just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks in the foundation, just a lot of quiet chatter in the corners. The usual signals are all green, but that doesn’t mean we should stop listening for the ones that aren’t."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old story on repeat. But the general’s words and the extra flights out of the city tell a different tale: the regime’s grip is iron, but the hands holding it are shaking."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual cracks are still there, but they’re being papered over with fresh paint, and the brushstrokes are too deliberate to ignore. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—something’s shifting, and it’s not just the weather."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
